 Nearly 20% of registered voters have cast ballots during Michigan’s early voting period so far
 Early voting will continue through Sunday, Nov. 1, for at least eight hours every day
 Jenny Sherman , Digital Content Producer
 Published:  October 28, 2026 at 10:06 AM Tags:  Decision 2026 , Early in-person voting , Michigan elections , Elections Early voters cast their ballots at Warren City Hall on Wednesday, Feb. 21, 2024, in Warren, Mich. (AP Photo/Carlos Osorio) (Carlos Osorio, Copyright 2024 The Associated Press. All rights reserved) The Nov. 3 General Election is only one week away, and nearly 20% of all active registered voters in Michigan have already cast their ballots, according to state officials.
 Early in-person voting opened statewide on Saturday, Oct. 24, attracting more than 215,000 voters to early voting sites across the state. 
 Recommended Videos
 Officials deem Michigan early in-person voting ‘a great success’
 Michigan’s Deputy Secretary of State Aghogho Edevbie said the first weekend of early in-person voting was “a great success,” with approximately 134,000 ballots cast across the state within the first 48 hours. This will be the first midterm general election where early in-person voting is an available option statewide, officials said.
 “Michigan voters are showing enthusiasm for early in-person voting,” Edevbie said in a news release on Tuesday. “Voters are using this convenient option to cast their ballot before polls open on Election Day. I want to thank our state’s dedicated local clerks and poll workers who helped make the success of this past weekend possible.” 
 Early voting will continue through Sunday, Nov. 1, for at least eight hours every day — with some communities offering additional early voting hours through Monday, Nov. 2. 
 Not sure where to find the closest early in-person voting site? You can view early in-person voting locations and times at mi.gov/earlyvoting .

 More than 1.1 million absentee ballots already counted
 As of Tuesday, Oct. 27, approximately 2,154,870 voters have requested an absentee ballot and 1,176,375 have returned them. The numbers mark a significant increase from the 1,899,273 voters who requested absentee ballots in the November 2022 General Election. Around 1,126,246 voters returned their ballot a week prior to the November 2022 election, officials said.
 Of the more than 2 million voters who already requested mail ballots for the upcoming election, 2,016,031 of them are on the permanent mail ballot list .
 Absentee ballots must be received by your local clerk’s office no later than 8 p.m. on election night (Nov. 3). Election officials recommend that anyone who has not yet mailed back their absentee ballot either use a local ballot drop box or hand-deliver it to the clerk’s office to avoid postal delays.
 Already mailed your ballot and not sure whether it’s been accepted? Voters can track the status of their ballot at mi.gov/trackballot .
